articles.title: Alex Scott: What does Disney+ exit highlight about coverage of women's football?
articles.summary: Alex Scott's sudden departure from her Disney+ presenter role reveals a pressing challenge for broadcasters of women's football.
articles.body:
On Thursday, former England footballer Alex Scott stepped away from Disney+'s coverage of the Women's Champions League after two rounds of matches.

The streaming giant is in the second season of a five-year deal to cover European football's flagship competition and this year introduced new formats, including a watchalong show with Scott alternating presenting duties with Shebahn Aherne.

However, it has had some technical issues and been criticised for a difficult opening night that included an unscheduled advert break during Arsenal's game against HB Koge.

Scott has not said why she left this role but told BBC Sport she was "grateful" for the opportunities she had at Disney+ and hoped to "continue working together" in the future.

But does her sudden departure highlight the challenges broadcasters face covering the women's game in an ever-changing media landscape?

Ad break in Women's Champions League was unscheduled

Broadcasters 'not sure who the audience is'

The explosion in interest in women's football during the past five years has been spearheaded by two of the biggest broadcasters in the UK – Sky Sports and the BBC.

In snapping up the Champions League before the 2025-26 season, Disney added its heft into the game, recognising its potential for capturing new audiences.

Indeed, Scott herself has launched her own YouTube show this season, One More Word WSL, which she presents on a Sunday night alongside ex-England internationals Anita Asante and Fara Williams.

Broadcasters have ramped up experiments with format, style and tone - Disney+ even had a dog on set during their coverage - but perhaps unsurprisingly, not every idea proves to be successful.

Journalist Carrie Dunn, who has covered women's sport for more than two decades, says opinions about coverage reflect a tension at the heart of the game.

"The challenge broadcasters are finding is that they are not sure who the audience is," she says. "A lot of it is targeted at a new generation and it's clearly not for people who have watched women's football for longer.

"Often it's a resourcing issue. Budgets are being cut and you're finding the same presenters and the same pundits trying to be all things to all people. It just doesn't work."

In the summer, the BBC announced its Women's Super League highlights show would not return for the 2026-27 season, but insisted it remained "fully committed to women's football".

To illustrate, it cited a bespoke new YouTube channel, the introduction of a debate show entitled The Women's Football Fallout, exclusively on BBC iPlayer, and the availability of clips and analysis on the BBC Sport website as evidence.

The decisions are part of a move away from linear television that the BBC says reflects changing audience habits.

It is a shift in emphasis that comes with difficulties.

"It's a tough balance where you've got to explain some context to the new fans without patronising your older fans," Dunn adds. "That's something the major broadcasters have not found a solution to yet.

"If people are willing to take risks on different kinds of women's sports coverage, that's fantastic.

"But start by choosing one thing and doing it really well – and that's got to be decent match coverage."

Watch The Women's Football Fallout on BBC iPlayer

Follow BBC Sport's Women's Football channel on YouTube

Bigger and more ambitious than ever - women's football on the BBC

Aston Villa interim boss Brian Sorensen started as a coach in Denmark in 2009 and believes the innovations in women's football coverage are a good thing, even if some do not always work.

"A lot of positive things are happening, but there are a lot of new areas that we haven't tried before," he said. "Sometimes it's trial and error and finding the right way for us.

"From when I started - with the worst live stream you've ever seen - to where we are now, is a very big improvement."

Andree Jeglertz, manager of champions Manchester City, agrees, acknowledging that the fact women's football has a much bigger audience now is a huge positive.

"I think the most important thing is that it is available and that people can see the best players on TV or live," he said. "The more, the better, no matter what."

Tottenham counterpart Martin Ho says the onus is on clubs and players to ensure the product on the field is worth watching.

"Whatever a broadcast partner decides to do, they have their reasons for it," he said. "All we can control is that we put on a good advert for women's football."

Finally, Chelsea's Sonia Bompastor suggested she was open to new expressions in covering the game provided they were properly analysed.

"Anytime you try to do something new, you will please some people and upset others," she told BBC Sport. "Sometimes you need to be patient and analyse as it is too soon to say if something is right or not."

articles.title: Lewis Koumas: Feel-good story gives Liverpool something to smile about
articles.summary: Lewis Koumas on breaking Steven Gerrard's record, seizing his opportunity under Andoni Iraola, and why he couldn't sleep after playing Manchester City.
articles.body:
The first player to celebrate with Lewis Koumas in front of the travelling supporters in Linz was Liverpool 's hat-trick hero in Bradley Barcola.

This time last season, Koumas was on loan at Birmingham in the Championship while Barcola was at Paris St-Germain, who went on to win the Champions League for the second season in a row.

Quite a chain of events led to the pair starting together for Liverpool in their 6-3 win over LASK.

And as Barcola left the Raiffeisen Arena with the match ball after a superb hat-trick, the Frenchman knew that he wasn't the only player who put the ball in the net three times on Wednesday in Austria.

Koumas had his first two strikes ruled out for offside, but thankfully it was third time luck for the 21-year-old Wales international.

And so, just three days after making his first Premier League start against Manchester City - with Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Hugo Ekitike all injured - Koumas became the youngest Liverpool player to score and assist in a Champions League game.

Previously, the youngest to achieve the feat had been Steven Gerrard in 2001.

When that was put to him, Koumas wanted to know "Is that official?".

"It's not a bad stat, is it?" he said. "And it's not a bad name to be alongside. Wow. What a legend. I just want more of this."

He is enjoying his run in the first team but staying level-headed about it all, keen to point out: "This is my job."

"I need to get goals and assists," he said. "I hadn't had any before Linz so it was really important to get them."

In a Liverpool side where attention tends to be directed towards big-money names, Koumas provides a real feel-good story.

He joined Liverpool aged 11 and scored on his first-team debut as an 18-year-old under Jurgen Klopp.

After spells on loan at Stoke, Birmingham and Hull , where he helped the Tigers win promotion last season, Andoni Iraola decided in the first week of pre-season that Koumas was part of his Liverpool plans.

He made his Premier League debut at Newcastle before coming on against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. He was man of the match on his first start of the season against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup after an energetic performance which left Iraola describing his playing style as "contagious".

That night, Koumas went straight on a video call with his family after the game and it was the case again in Austria after he scored his first goal of the season.

"It was probably the best feeling in my career, 100%. I'm just really grateful to have the opportunity again," said Koumas.

"I would not have been a happy man [if I didn't score], I would have been gutted. I just kept going because I knew the more the game was going on, it was opening up.

"Going over to the fans at the end meant absolutely everything. They are the reason we do this and that we want this job. I wish I could have got in there with them, but there was a big metal cage in the way!"

'I couldn't sleep after the Man City game'

It has been quite a week for the son of former Wales midfielder Jason Koumas.

Young Koumas has started two Liverpool games in a row, and on Sunday he nearly scored his first Premier League goal.

At 0-0 against Manchester City , Barcola played him through and Koumas connected sweetly but Gianluigi Donnarumma kept his effort out in front of the Kop.

Koumas was "absolutely gutted" the ball did not ripple the back of the net.

"I couldn't really sleep [on Sunday]. I just kept thinking about the chance all night. I feel like I couldn't have hit it any better. The keeper is huge and he was just in the right place and I think in normal circumstances it goes in."

While Koumas has an important role for now, he knows the likes of Isak and Gakpo will soon be back in first-team contention.

"You never know when your last game is going to be," Koumas said. "I know that sounds like a cliche, but it is true.

"I have got to keep pushing, every chance I get."

Koumas could lead Liverpool 's attack for the third time in seven days when Liverpool travel to Brentford on Saturday.

Iraola said on Thursday that it was "too early" to tell whether Isak or Gakpo would be available.

The fact it would not be a surprise if Koumas starts again is testament to the impression he has made on Iraola. The manner in which he is seizing his opportunity is inspiring others too.

Liverpool 's under-19s beat LASK's youngsters 4-2 in their Uefa Youth League game on Wednesday, with 18-year-old Will Wright scoring a hat-trick.

"You see Koumas with the first team and the energy he brings to the front line - that's from being in the academy, and Will has a similar identity," said Rob Page, Liverpool 's academy boss.

"We have a manager who has come in and has an identity about how he wants to play which suits a lot of the players. And they've seen a pathway there now: Rio [Ngumoha], Trey [Nyoni] and now Koumas.

"My message was 'where is the next one coming from? So go and show the manager what you are capable of doing'," Page said.

"We are getting chances but, ultimately, it is because we are good enough. Trey and Rio are unbelievable and, if you're good enough it doesn't matter how old you are," said Koumas.

First-team duty for the 20-time English champions could become the norm for the academy graduates.

"Hopefully that is the case and that's how I would love it to go," said Koumas, "but you just have to keep working hard, keep my head down and doing what the gaffer asks of me and make it last as long as we can."

articles.summary: El regreso del extremo al trabajo con sus compañeros se suma al de Pedrola, mientras Calero espera concretar qué jugadores tendrá disponibles en Ceuta
articles.body: Las bandas del Oviedo empiezan a ofrecer un respiro a Julián Calero. Después de semanas de contratiempos físicos entre sus jugadores de ataque, el técnico contó este viernes con Ilyas Chaira en el trabajo con el grupo. El extremo avanza en la recuperación de la lesión de hombro que sufrió en el amistoso frente al Deportivo en julio, aunque su incorporación al entrenamiento todavía no garantiza su disponibilidad para competir. Chaira se suma a Estanis Pedrola, que también continúa ejercitándose con sus compañeros. Son dos pasos que acercan al entrenador la posibilidad de ampliar sus alternativas por fuera, una zona especialmente castigada por las lesiones en este inicio de temporada. El regreso a las listas dependerá de cómo completen ambos el proceso de recuperación. La visita del domingo al Ceuta mantiene otros interrogantes más inmediatos. Precisamente los ex caballas Youness y Aisar tenían previsto participar en alguna parte de la sesión de El Requexón para comprobar sus sensaciones. De su respuesta al esfuerzo dependerán sus opciones de estar a disposición de Calero para el encuentro del Alfonso Murube. También aguarda su oportunidad Brandon Domingues. El atacante acumula trabajo con el equipo, pero sigue sin recibir el alta médica. Ișfan, por su parte, encara la recta final de su recuperación muscular y tiene pendiente incorporarse a los entrenamientos con sus compañeros. El panorama ofrece avances, aunque la enfermería todavía condiciona las decisiones de Calero. Chris Ramos, Juan Cruz y Carlos Fernández necesitarán más tiempo para regresar y continúan entre las bajas de mayor recorrido. El entrenamiento deja así una noticia favorable con Ilyas Chaira como protagonista, pero sin resolver aún cuántos efectivos podrá recuperar el Oviedo para Ceuta. El cuerpo técnico deberá valorar la evolución de los futbolistas que se acercan al regreso antes de concretar la convocatoria.

articles.title: Man City charges: Do Premier League club have grounds for their appeal?
articles.summary: Manchester City face "substantial hurdles" to overcome if they are to have any chance of winning their appeal after being found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules, a leading lawyer has told BBC Sport.
articles.body:
Manchester City face "substantial hurdles" if they are to have any chance of winning their appeal after being found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules, a leading lawyer has told BBC Sport.

City have been found guilty of all charges related to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, and creating "sham contracts" to inflate sponsorship deals by £830m.

The club have said they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League" and they have "irrefutable evidence" the ruling "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe".

In their appeal, City will argue the payments were made by the United Arab Emirates government as a shareholder of the sponsors, while there are inconsistencies in the Commission's judgement.

Therefore, City say the sponsorship amounts were legitimate and not topped up by the owners.

James Severn, Member of the London Solicitor Litigation Association (LSLA) and Partner at Penningtons Manches Cooper, told BBC Sport the appeal is "not simply an opportunity to invite a new panel" to get the verdict overturned.

"City will need to identify a material error of law, principle or fact, or serious procedural unfairness, which materially affected the Commission's decision," Severn said.

"The Appeal Board nevertheless has broad powers to allow or dismiss the appeal, vary the decision or make any other order it considers appropriate."

City must prove available evidence was misinterpreted

Etihad Airways, one of City's principle sponsors at the centre of the case, had previously stated that the Abu Dhabi government had not paid for its sponsorship of Manchester City .

That came in court documents as part of a US investigation in New York in 2015.

City will argue this does not have the full context of the situation and is not proof they have been inconsistent with evidence.

The club are adamant government documents fully support their case - but, Severn said, if these were already available to the Commission they may not be much use in an appeal.

"The bank statements, government records and contemporaneous payment documents could be powerful evidence if they establish a clear audit trail showing the disputed funds came from the Abu Dhabi government rather than the owners," Severn added.

"However, if that evidence was already before the Commission, which nevertheless concluded that the arrangements were a sham, City will face an uphill struggle to demonstrate the finding was materially wrong."

Shortly before City's appeal was confirmed, Etihad Airways issued a statement saying it had never been "given the opportunity by the Premier League to be represented, to provide relevant information, or to ensure the accuracy and fairness of information relied upon".

Severn said Etihad Airways' complaint "does not, of itself, establish procedural unfairness".

"Etihad was not the respondent and is unlikely to have had an independent right to participate in the proceedings," Severn said. "It is likely to have been open to either party to obtain and present such evidence to the Commission.

"If the Appeal Board is prepared to consider new evidence from Etihad, it is likely to carry greater weight if supported by contemporaneous documents."

How much did Man City's rule breaking cost your team?

Were any current Man City players signed during charges period?

Manchester City’s inflatable banana craze

City could argue a 'material factual error'

A key part of City's defence will be that the Independent Commission relied too heavily on the emails obtained through the Football Leaks files.

"If City can demonstrate the Commission fundamentally misunderstood the emails, failed to consider their proper context or reached conclusions inconsistent with other contemporaneous documents, that could amount to a material factual error," Severn added.

"City's difficulty is that the Commission heard extensive witness and documentary evidence but nevertheless made serious findings of sham arrangements and disguised owner funding."

Kieran Maguire, professor of football finance at the University of Liverpool , told BBC Sport the commission found "the documents were retrofitted to fit the crime".

"The Commission must have concluded that the evidence and the credibility of the witnesses put up by Manchester City were poor," Maguire said.

"However, from a legal point of view, this is an area they could attack if Manchester City 's team can prove that the commission itself was a flawed construct in the sense that the members were Premier League picks rather than Manchester City 's, and therefore the deck was stacked against the club to begin with.

Severn added that the retired senior judges and leading barristers, who sat on the Commission, have "spent their careers interpreting complicated facts, dealing with witnesses and applying relevant weight to evidence".

While adding that it would be "impossible to assess reliably" the chances of City winning their appeal, Severn added that "doing so will not be easy".

But Maguire believes that while it will be difficult for City to be successful, "there is a route".

City have brought in Mark Howard KC to advise the club in their appeal, while Etihad Airways has enlisted the services of respected law firm Quinn Emanuel.

Maguire said: "Given the lawyers that have been recruited by Manchester City , they may go down what's been described to me as a mess and noise approach.

"That means trying to discredit everything to do with the process of the Commission rather than necessarily the evidence that was presented.

"I've seen the documents that Abu Dhabi presented to the New York case. I'm not a lawyer, but from an accounting point of view, they can be seen in more than one way."

Even though Premier League regulations state an appeal must be heard within 12 weeks, or by Christmas Eve, Severn added that "given the scale and complexity of the proceedings, a final outcome may not be known for some time".

articles.title: Spain to appeal to CAS after FIFA penalty for Islamophobic chants
articles.summary: Spain appeals to Court of Arbitration for Sport following FIFA sanctions for fans’ behaviour during Egypt friendly.
articles.body:
Spain’s football federation is taking its case to ⁠the Court of Arbitration for Sport after FIFA rejected an appeal against sanctions imposed for Islamophobic chants by supporters during a match against Egypt in March.

FIFA fined the ⁠federation (RFEF) $20,000 and ordered it to close at least 15% of the available seats for Spain’s next home friendly.

The sanctions follow incidents at the RCDE Stadium near Barcelona, home of LaLiga club Espanyol, where ⁠ some Spain fans chanted , “If you don’t jump, you’re a Muslim” during the goalless World Cup warm-up match.

After the second occurrence of the chant, the stadium announcer issued a warning and the scoreboard displayed a message against discriminatory behaviour.

Spain winger Lamine Yamal, who is Muslim, condemned the chants at ‌the time, describing them as disrespectful and intolerable and calling those responsible “ignorant and racist”.

Spanish police launched an investigation the following day while world governing body FIFA later started disciplinary proceedings against the RFEF.

The RFEF argued that the word ‘Muslim’ was “neither insulting nor pejorative”, adding the fans’ conduct should be assessed under FIFA’s Article 17, which covers political, ideological, religious or offensive messages, rather than Article 15, which deals with discrimination and racist abuse.

FIFA’s disciplinary committee rejected that argument, saying Article 15 ⁠does not require the explicit use of a slur and that a ⁠term can be discriminatory when used in context as “an insult, taunt, or marker of inferiority”.

The RFEF appealed the sanction, but a FIFA spokesperson told Reuters that it was dismissed last week, prompting the Spanish federation to take the ⁠case to CAS, the highest authority in sports disputes.

“Throughout the proceedings, the RFEF has maintained that it acted immediately, diligently and effectively from the moment ⁠it became aware of the incidents,” a high-ranking official in the ⁠RFEF told Reuters.

“Furthermore, the measures taken ensured that the chants were not repeated and that the spectators present in the stadium themselves expressed their disapproval of such behaviour.”

The official said the federation considered the sanctions particularly severe, arguing that comparable capacity restrictions ‌had not been imposed automatically in more serious cases or those involving previous disciplinary offences.

The chants were detected by the RFEF’s monitoring systems and immediately reported to the match ‌officials, ‌the official said, adding that security was reinforced in the affected section of the stadium.

“The federation cooperated fully with the relevant authorities to identify those responsible.”

El técnico Luis García sigue teniendo las bajas de larga duración de Manu Morlanes y Antoniu Roca. articles.title: Aranbarri avisa: "El Mallorca es un equipo poderoso y muy completo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Eibar sólo cuenta con la baja de Sergio Álvarez y tendrá que hacer un descarte para retomar la senda de las victorias
articles.summary: El técnico del Eibar sólo cuenta con la baja de Sergio Álvarez y tendrá que hacer un descarte para retomar la senda de las victorias
articles.body: Ni las siete victorias seguidas cambiaron el discurso de Jokin Aranbarri ni el tropiezo del lunes en el Carlos Tartiere lo ha hecho. El técnico del Eibar mantiene el buen semblante y sabe de la importancia de volver a ofrecer la mejor versión ante el Mallorca este sábado. Sólo así su equipo será capaz de doblegar a uno de los grandes candidatos al ascenso. Un encuentro de poder a poder que supondrá un examen de altura para el equipo azulgrana. "El objetivo es demostrar lo que somos, lo que queremos ser y en qué estamos mejorando" destacó el míster armero "Es un equipo poderoso. Sin balón es capaz de presionar alto y se siente cómodo porque es físicamente fuerte. Cuando lo hundes un poco, defiende bien el área y es contundente. Con balón tiene extremos y delanteros son muy verticales. No necesita dominar durante mucho tiempo porque tiene capacidad para hacer daño rápido. Por dentro tiene capacidad para asociarse y cuenta con buenos jugadores con tiro desde fuera del área. Es un equipo muy completo", reflexiona Aranbarri sobre las virtudes del Mallorca. El preparador armero ve preparados a sus jugadores para la batalla. "Lo que más me gusta del equipo es que tiene fuego interior y quiere ir a por las cosas. En Oviedo, en un contexto exigente y en un estadio que apretaba, empezamos perdiendo y la imagen que dimos fue de querer demostrar que vamos a por las cosas. Eso es difícil de conseguir y muy fácil de perder, porque cuando los resultados no llegan, es complicado mantenerlo. La fuerza del equipo en ese sentido es muy grande. Ese fuego interior que tenemos tiene mucho valor", sostiene. Volver a Ipurua después de disputar cuatro de los últimos cinco encuentros a domicilio también supone un estímulo. "Siempre es bueno jugar en Ipurua. En Oviedo tuvimos a mucha gente animándonos y, hace dos semanas, también hubo mucho apoyo en casa desde el inicio. Ya se sentía algo especial. No es casualidad que el equipo salga tan enchufado y fuerte, ni que hayamos hecho un partido tan completo contra Las Palmas. Ipurua, con nuestra gente, es especial".

articles.title: Arda y Bernardo piden sitio
articles.standfirst: Claves en la remontada ante la Roma, se reivindicaron ante un Mourinho que volvió a apostar por el doble pivote Fede-Tchouaméni
articles.summary: Claves en la remontada ante la Roma, se reivindicaron ante un Mourinho que volvió a apostar por el doble pivote Fede-Tchouaméni
articles.body: El partido ante la Roma evidenció que José Mourinho tienen muy clara la formación de su centro del campo tipo. El entrenador portugués apostó, una vez, por el doble pivote formado por Fede Valverde y Aurélien Tchouaméni. El resultado fue decepcionante, hasta el punto de que, en el primer tiempo, el futbolista elegido para iniciar el juego en el Madrid no fue ni el uruguayo ni el francés. Esa tarea recayó en Thibaut Courtois, que, colocado entre los centrales, intentó hasta 19 pases largo, más que los dos futbolistas, en teoría, encargados de dar sentido al juego del Madrid. No funcionó, ni en el primer tiempo ni en el arranque del segundo, en el que la Roma, a través de Malen, logró una renta de dos goles (3-1) que pareció finiquitar el partido. Viéndolo perdido, Mou revolucionó su once, dando entrada en primer lugar a Arda Güler (minuto 59) y más tarde a Bernardo Silva (70'). La salida del turco desplazó a Valverde al lateral derecho, una demarcación en la que ya fue decisivo ante el Villarreal. El portugués salió directamente por Tchouaméni, formando un doble pivote radicalmente distinto al que arrancó el partido. Con Arda y Bernardo, el Madrid se hizo con el control del balón y acabó remontando gracias a dos asistencias directas del turco, que además participó de forma activa en el gol de Espí. El delantero valenciano y Endrick fueron las otras notas positivas de la reacción de los blancos. Ambos anotaron y llevaron al área romanista una sensación de peligro de la que, de nuevo, estuvo muy lejos Vinicius, titular apenas un par de horas después de conocer su sanción de cuatro partidos en Liga. El brasileño fue, junto a Dumfries, el primer jugador desmovilizado por su entrenador, en una vuelta de tuerca radical que acabó valiendo tres muy valiosos puntos en el Olímpico. Pese al cambio radical del equipo con las entradas de Arda y Bernardo, Mou se resistió en rueda de prensa a anticipar una continuidad en esa idea. De manera contundente, además. "Si empezamos como acabamos, nos meten cinco. Hay momentos y momentos. Tenía cambios para hacer. Se iban a cansar, iban a llegar las tarjetas", dijo el técnico del Madrid al ser preguntado por el cambio de guion aparejado a sus cambios en Roma. Unas declaraciones que parecen reforzar su idea de apostar por un centro del campo más físico y de menos toque en los próximos partidos, empezando por el del domingo ante el Sevilla. Además, una de las claves de ese posible cambio de modelo pasa por la posición de Fede Valverde. En los dos últimos partidos, el charrúa ha tenido más incidencia en el juego desde el lateral que en el centro del campo. Un viejo debate que lleva tiempo instalado en el Real Madrid, a pesar de que el futbolista se mostró abiertamente en contra de un cambio de posición hace más o menos un año, todavía con Xabi Alonso como entrenador del Madrid. El miércoles, el capitán del Madrid fue menos refractario a la idea. "Lo importante es ganar, como dijo el míster. Si las cosas salen bien hay que salir adelante y yo feliz de seguir teniendo minutos sea donde sea, disfruto mucho jugando, tenía mucho espacio para correr en banda y agradecido a que el míster siga confiando en mí y yo daré el máximo por el equipo", dijo un Valverde cuyo cambio de posición fue descartado por Mourinho en la previa del partido de Roma. "Si tienes más de un Fede lo haces jugar de lateral, en el centro del campo... Pero como solo tenemos un Fede, verle de lateral es algo muy específico", dijo el de Setúbal. Un posible cambio de posición de Fede dejaría libre una plaza en el centro del campo, abriendo las puertas a una medular de más control y menos músculo. La fórmula que funcionó en Roma, en una situación desesperada de la que el Madrid salió gracias a Güler y Bernardo, dos futbolistas que piden paso en el Madrid. La pelota, en el tejado de Mou.

articles.body:
Erling Haaland Rest Decision Puts Man City Rotation Under Spotlight

Manchester City have a straightforward issue to manage before Ipswich arrive at the Etihad. Erling Haaland keeps scoring, keeps starting and keeps piling up minutes. Eventually, that catches up with you.

Enzo Maresca has now said the quiet part out loud. "At some point we probably need to give him rest, some days off," the Italian said in his pre-match press conference on Friday. That does not confirm Haaland will sit out the Ipswich game, but it plainly puts the idea on the table.

Haaland workload becoming hard to ignore

The schedule has been relentless. Haaland has featured for City across three competitions and missed only the Carabao Cup third round win over Norwich. He also started all four of Norway's Nations League matches during the autumn international break.

There was already a fitness concern after he limped off against Portugal on October 4. Since then, he has done what elite centre-forwards do, he recovered, played, and scored. He found the net against Liverpool and then struck twice in the Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain. That leaves him on 13 goals for club and country this season.

He has also scored in seven consecutive matches for City. Form is not the problem. Fatigue might be.

Maresca made clear this is not solely about Haaland. "We are thinking about this not just with Erling because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams.

"Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernandez], Marc [Guehi], Erling, Ruben [Dias] – so at some point we probably need to give them some rest."

That is sensible squad management, nothing more, nothing less. The question is timing.

Ipswich test may come too soon for full rest

On balance, leaving Haaland out against Ipswich would still feel unlikely. City can go six points clear at the top, temporarily at least, with a win. Managers do not usually bench their most decisive player in that situation unless they have to.

The more logical window for rotation may be the upcoming European fixture against AEK Athens. City also lack a like-for-like replacement. Antoine Semenyo can lead the line and Phil Foden can operate as a false nine, as seen in previous seasons, but neither gives opponents the same problem.

For now, the message is simple. Haaland needs protecting, City need points, and Maresca has a call to make.

articles.title: Graeme Souness sends warning to Liverpool over ‘fragile’ duo
articles.summary: Alexander Isak Injury Concern Grows as Bradley Barcola Delivers Liverpool BreakthroughLiverpool finally got a return that looked worthy of a nine-figure outl...
articles.body:
Alexander Isak Injury Concern Grows as Bradley Barcola Delivers Liverpool Breakthrough

Liverpool finally got a return that looked worthy of a nine-figure outlay. Bradley Barcola's Champions League hat-trick against LASK was emphatic, timely and badly needed. More to the point, it felt like the first genuinely weighty statement from Liverpool's expensive attacking rebuild.

Alexander Isak had started the season well before his latest injury setback. Florian Wirtz has shown flashes without fully taking hold of games. Barcola, though, produced the kind of night that cuts through the noise. Three goals, a proper European headline, and a reminder that top-end talent eventually has to deliver more than promise.

That said, one big night for Barcola does not solve Liverpool's broader issue. The concern remains availability, especially around Isak and Hugo Ekitike. Talent has never been the argument. Fitness is.

With Liverpool heading to Brentford, Andoni Iraola has decisions to make. Isak has missed the last two matches after being available for the opening seven of the campaign. Given the way Liverpool attacked in Austria, it is fair to assume he would have fancied his chances of scoring had he been involved. Iraola has suggested there is a possibility the striker could return this weekend, but that still feels uncertain rather than imminent.

Alexander Isak fitness remains central issue

The problem with Isak is obvious. When he plays, he scores and lifts the attack. When he does not, the discussion immediately turns to whether Liverpool can trust his body over the length of a season. That is not unfair, it is the reality of his career so far.

The warning has now been laid out bluntly by Graeme Souness: "I mean the players they brought in have not really performed to the levels they would want." That is harsh on Barcola after his hat-trick and arguably premature on Wirtz, but it gets to the larger point. Expensive forwards are judged over months, not moments.

On Isak and Ekitike, the verdict was even sharper: "Isak is fragile, but they knew that when they bought him, Ekitike is fragile and if they continue being like that then they've got problems.

"They are goal scorers, you know Isak can score goals in the Premier League and he will get goals for them, but how many games will they play in a season? Wirtz is yet to really, really get going."

That is hard to dismiss. Ekitike is still recovering from the Achilles rupture suffered in April and is not expected back for a couple of months. Liverpool therefore have two high-level forwards with clear medical question marks attached. If that pattern continues, the squad planning starts to look risky rather than bold.

Bradley Barcola gives Liverpool a timely lift

Barcola's treble matters because it changes the conversation, at least briefly. Before Wednesday, most of the scrutiny had fallen on Wirtz, partly because Isak has been unavailable and partly because big fees always demand immediate impact. Barcola now has his defining early-season moment.

Liverpool needed that. A front line built at massive cost cannot spend all season waiting for everyone to be fit at once. Someone has to seize games. Against LASK, Barcola did exactly that.

There is still work to do. One hat-trick does not prove the attacking unit is settled, and it does not answer the question of how Liverpool function when Isak and Ekitike are missing. It does, however, provide a glimpse of what this side can look like when one of the expensive additions truly clicks.

Andoni Iraola wants intensity without excuses

Iraola has also been backed for the clarity of his messaging. "I have to say, I like the manager," came the assessment. "Because I lived down in Poole I used to go down and watch Bournemouth. He plays front-footed football, likeable guy when you hear him speak, it's all common sense which is a rarity these days, rather than all the gobbledygook which coaches and managers spout.

"I like him, so I'm hoping so [that Liverpool can get back to their best], because he seems to be a good guy. I just feel when I look at Liverpool that maybe the midfield is not as good at doing the hard yards, the hard yards in football are when you don't have the ball, and it makes the back four vulnerable.

"People talk about the back four but sometimes it's the people in front who are not closing the ball down properly all of the time. If there's five of you doing it, five have to do it. If four do it and one of you goes to sleep, you'll be vulnerable."

That assessment is straightforward and accurate. Liverpool's issues are not limited to injured forwards. Defensive exposure often starts higher up the pitch. Iraola's teams are built on pressure, work and collective responsibility. If one player switches off, the system breaks.

Barcola gave Liverpool a headline in Europe. Brentford away will be a different test. The bigger questions, around Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and whether this team can sustain intensity, remain unanswered.

articles.title: Elyaz Zidane: "Quiero escribir mi propia historia"
articles.standfirst: El hijo de la leyenda francesa habló sobre su carrera y el peso de su apellido en una entrevista
articles.summary: El hijo de la leyenda francesa habló sobre su carrera y el peso de su apellido en una entrevista
articles.body: Zinedine Zidane fue uno de los mejores jugadores de la historia. Pero su apellido siempre ha tenido un gran peso en sus descendientes, poniendo en ellos grandes expectativas. Su hijo pequeño, Elyaz Zidane, busca construir su propio legado. Como afirmó en una entrevista a Le Parisien, el pequeño de los Zidane prefiere utilizar su propio nombre en la camiseta en lugar de los apellidos. "En el Real Betis, mi camiseta llevaba impreso 'Elyaz'. Quería mantener esa costumbre, sin ninguna intención de esconderme tras mi nombre. El fútbol siempre ha sido algo natural en nuestra familia. Habiendo estado inmerso en el mundo del fútbol desde muy pequeño, era natural que quisiera seguir sus pasos. Pero quiero escribir mi propia historia", cuenta. Cuando le preguntan sobre si es más fácil o difícil ser hijo de una leyenda como Zinedine, Elyaz responde que es una combinación de ambas. "Es una mezcla de ambas cosas. Hay aspectos positivos, pero también otros más complejos, sobre todo la constante comparación y el hecho de ser juzgado con mayor severidad que los demás. Cuando eres joven, lo más importante es poder desarrollarte sin estar constantemente bajo la lupa, y eso fue un poco difícil. Pero, por otro lado, estoy sumamente orgulloso de mi padre, quien me transmitió muchos consejos. Siempre estuvo ahí para apoyarme", dice. El futbolista que se ha unido al Estrella Roja todavía tiene mucho futuro por delante. "Estaba muy feliz de unirme a un club histórico como el Estrella Roja, apoyado por una afición fantástica que siempre está ahí para nosotros. Tomé la decisión correcta. Aunque mi formación futbolística es profundamente española tras mis años de entrenamiento allí, quería absorber la mentalidad francesa. A los 20 años, todo es posible. Me niego a presionarme y prefiero concentrarme en el campo. Mi único objetivo ahora mismo es darlo todo por el Estrella Roja, mejorar y ayudar a mi equipo a ganar. El resto está por escribirse.", finaliza.

articles.title: Grego Sierra, el valor de quedarse
articles.standfirst: Central de oficio, carácter y experiencia, cumplirá ante el Sabadell, su ex equipo, 150 partidos de Liga como futbolista del Burgos
articles.summary: Central de oficio, carácter y experiencia, cumplirá ante el Sabadell, su ex equipo, 150 partidos de Liga como futbolista del Burgos
articles.body: Hay futbolistas que dejan huella por sus goles y otros que construyen su historia desde un lugar menos vistoso, lejos de los focos que suelen iluminar a los protagonistas del marcador. Grego Sierra pertenece a ese segundo grupo. Central de oficio, carácter y experiencia, el murciano se ha convertido en uno de los rostros reconocibles del Burgos CF, una camiseta que volverá a defender este domingo ante el Sabadell con una cifra redonda: 150 partidos de Liga como blanquinegro. El registro tiene un significado especial para un jugador que, cuando aterrizó en Burgos en el verano de 2021, difícilmente podía imaginar todo lo que estaba por venir. El equipo regresaba a Segunda división después de dos décadas de ausencia y comenzaba una etapa en la que cada temporada suponía un nuevo desafío. Sierra llegó para ayudar a consolidar al conjunto en el fútbol profesional y terminó formando parte de una de las etapas más reconocibles de su historia reciente. El camino, sin embargo, no empezó de la manera que habría deseado. El propio futbolista recuerda con humor aquel estreno complicado, marcado por un gol en propia puerta frente al Leganés. Una anécdota que ha quedado atrás y que contrasta con el peso que ha adquirido desde entonces dentro del vestuario. "No esperaba en ese momento alcanzar la cifra de partidos que he jugado aquí ni aguantar tanto tiempo", reconocía esta semana. Su explicación para entender la continuidad es más sencilla que cualquier análisis táctico: se siente querido. La primera misión de Grego Sierra en Burgos consistió en ayudar a asegurar la permanencia. El objetivo se cumplió con solvencia durante la campaña 2021-22, pero el siguiente curso elevó las expectativas. El conjunto dirigido por Julián Calero encontró en la organización defensiva una de sus principales señas de identidad y el central murciano se convirtió en una pieza importante de aquella estructura. En la temporada 2022-23, el Burgos protagonizó una de las historias defensivas más destacadas del fútbol profesional español. José Antonio Caro estableció un récord de imbatibilidad y el trabajo colectivo de la zaga resultó fundamental para sostener aquella trayectoria. Sierra fue uno de los integrantes de un bloque que hizo de la disciplina, la concentración y la solidaridad sus principales argumentos. El verano de 2024 abrió un paréntesis, aunque breve, en su historia burgalesa. Después de tres temporadas consecutivas y 87 encuentros oficiales con el equipo, Sierra emprendió una nueva aventura en el Universitatea Craiova rumano. El cambio de escenario le permitió conocer otro fútbol, aunque su estancia lejos de El Plantío apenas se prolongó durante unos meses. En enero de 2025 regresó al Burgos. No era una incorporación cualquiera: volvía un jugador que conocía el club, la categoría y las exigencias de una competición en la que la experiencia puede marcar diferencias. Este hecho no le permite ser el jugador con más temporadas consecutivas en el equipo, sin embargo, lo convirtió en un fijo en la zaga burgalesa. La segunda etapa confirmó que su relación con el Burgos no había quedado cerrada con aquella despedida. Sierra recuperó protagonismo y volvió a desempeñar un papel importante en la defensa, aportando contundencia, conocimiento del juego y liderazgo. Ahora, en su sexta temporada vinculada a la entidad, forma parte del grupo de futbolistas que representan la continuidad dentro de una plantilla sometida a cambios constantes. La celebración de sus 150 partidos llegará, además, ante un adversario que ocupa un lugar especial en su trayectoria. El Sabadell fue su equipo entre 2019 y 2021, antes de su llegada a Burgos. Allí disfrutó de una etapa importante de su carrera, consiguió el ascenso a Segunda División y estableció vínculos personales que todavía conserva. Una de sus hijas nació durante aquellos años en Cataluña. "Va a ser un partido especial entre dos equipos que tengo en mi corazón", explicaba el defensa. La coincidencia añade un componente sentimental a una jornada que ya tiene suficiente valor por la cifra que alcanzará. Pero Sierra también sabe que, una vez que comience el encuentro, los recuerdos tendrán que dejar paso a la competición. El objetivo es sumar los tres puntos y ofrecer una alegría a la afición.

articles.title: Martin O'Neill: As Hearts test awaits, is Celtic manager right to be 'delighted' despite Benfica defeat?
articles.summary: Celtic have lost four of their last five matches in all competitions; Martin O'Neill's side return to action against last season's Premiership runners up Hearts in their first Parkhead meeting since their final-day decider; watch Celtic vs Hearts live on Sky Sports from 2.30pm on Sunday
articles.body:
However, is the 74-year-old right to be "really, really delighted" with the Hoops' second-half performance in Lisbon?

The result leaves Celtic with no points from six after two league-phase fixtures in the Europa League and means they have now lost four of their last five matches across all competitions.

Another defeat - fairly or unfairly - also raises more questions over O'Neill's future in the Parkhead hot seat.

It was just weeks ago, following consecutive defeats to Rangers and a loss in their opening Europa League fixture, that O'Neill said he was going to consider his position after a gruelling week. He stayed, and now he must deliver.

Here we answer some key questions as the veteran boss chases another huge result on Sunday...

Following that 4-1 thumping against Benfica , O'Neill hailed Celtic's second-half display and believes they can still progress in the competition despite sitting 34th in a 36-team table.

"The last thing you want to do is concede so early on," he told TNT Sports . "Then at 2-0 we've got a great, great chance to make it 2-1 and within a few minutes they make it 3-0.

"We could have capitulated, but I thought the second-half performance was really terrific. It was a game of two halves. We created chance after chance, we should have scored more goals.

"The second-half performance gives me what I would call the determination, and I think we can still qualify. I know it's down to six games, but we want to qualify for this competition to get into the knockout stages.

"Overall, I'm really, really delighted with the second-half performance, and it's a shame that we conceded the three goals first of all."

Benfica were clinical and ultimately too much to handle.

In the first half, even when Celtic were not causing their own problems, such as giving away a penalty for the hosts' opener, they were being cut apart at times. That's where the problem lies.

Yes, O'Neill's side could have scored when they hit the frame of the goal in either half - but so could have their opponents.

Yes, things did improve after the restart - but could it have got any worse considering the Hoops were 3-0 down after 36 minutes?

O'Neill may be using all of his managerial experience to try to motivate his side and create some positivity among the fans ahead of a huge game against Hearts. After all, he needs a raucous Parkhead on Sunday to help them get past last season's runners-up.

So those with a glass half-full mindset will be fully in favour of that. However, those with a glass half-empty approach will have been worried by Thursday and demand improvement. Quickly.

Losing in their Champions League qualifier, to Rangers in the Premiership and League Cup, and now another Europa League loss - the worrying trend of failure in big matches is something that needs to end.

Speaking on Sky Sports News, Tino Callaghan from A Celtic Exchange Podcast said:

"They were the kind of comments I suppose you'd expect any manager to make. There are small positives to take from Celtic's second half, and I think the manager is choosing to accentuate them, which you would expect him to do.

"However, there was so much wrong in the first half in particular, and that's where the real issues are for Celtic at this moment in time.

"It's just the fact that at times we weren't even competing. We were completely outstripped in that first half, and I think that in itself points back to a more general feeling of frustration amongst the fans that we are no longer competing at the top table in Europe.

"Back in the day, we would potentially draw Benfica in the Champions League and fancy our chances of maybe getting something, but we went into that game last night with no real hope.

"I really thought he was going to leave after his comments after the Rangers game. They were particularly concerning. It's not that everyone else was asking the question. The man himself was asking the question of himself, and I thought there was a serious chance he would walk.

"It seems that he's taken some time to reflect. He's probably spoken to people at the club and decided to stay on, but you need to start getting results if you've decided that you are the man for the job.

"Hearts is massive now on Sunday. A must-win game. Martin O'Neill came out quite strongly, saying that he thinks we still can qualify in the Europa League too. I agree with that, but talk is cheap. You need to start doing it on the park, and that starts again on Sunday."

Sutton: What does O'Neill have going for him?

Speaking before Celtic beat Motherwell, former Parkhead player and Sky Sports pundit Chris Sutton said:

"I thought he was wrong to say what he said in terms of he had doubts [about his future in the job]. People will view that as a weakness. I think that was a big mistake.

"I've never heard him talk like that in his whole managerial career. I just think, if I was Martin, I would just want an easy life. What has he got going for him at Celtic at this moment?

"He didn't get the players he wanted in order to compete at the highest of levels in Europe, so he was let down there. He was undermined by one of his players, Cameron Carter-Vickers, who shouldn't be coming out publicly and undermining the manager and questioning the tactics.

"It just shows where the club is at. It's like the Wild West, there are shots fired everywhere. You now have the situation where the Green Brigade are saying 'we are not going to rock up at European games. We aren't going to go to the cup games.'

"The split between the top of the club and the supporters, I thought couldn't get any wider than last year. It does seem now that it is more fractious."

articles.body: Martín Pascual pasa por uno de sus mejores momentos de su carrera futbolística. Al central madrileño le ha sentado de maravilla cambiar de aires y en el Dinamo de Bucarest, equipo de la Liga I de Rumanía, su presencia es casi imprescindible y el equipo es el líder y menos goleado de la Primera rumana. El defensa madrileño es un fijo en el once del técnico portugués Nuno Campos y se ha convertido en el Pichichi al llevar cinco goles en este inicio liguero. Sin duda, los datos goleadores de Martín Pascual casi igualan a los que obtuvo cuando jugaba en los juveniles del Rayo Vallecano. Y es que el defensa siempre tuvo alma de delantero. Por su gran inicio liguero, al central le están siguiendo, muy de cerca, equipos de MLS y de la Bundesliga. Su colocación, visión del juego, adelantarse a los rivales, buscar el hueco exacto, envergadura y dominio del juego aéreo, entre otras cualidades, son claves para que el ex del Rayo Vallecano se convierta en 'El Matador' (así le llaman en el equipo) del Dinamo de Bucarest. Y es que Martín está demostrando su gran potencial en un vestuario donde, a pesar de las múltiples nacionalidades, todo se habla en inglés. En jugadas a balón parado es clave, ya que con su presencia hace 'temblar' a los rivales y da confianza a los suyos, así como en cualquier jugada que el defensa español se sume al ataque. Él tiene claro cuál es su función sobre el rectángulo de juego, pero aprovecha a la perfección la libertad que tiene, y cuando la ocasión es la idónea, para encarar la meta rival. Y es que su gran criterio en la salida de balón es una de las claves del equipo. Su liderazgo está por encima de todo. Sus cinco goles en la Primera de Rumanía le hacen ser, en la actualidad, el quinto español con más goles marcados en esta categoría en todas las ligas del mundo. Un dato que, para ser central y teniendo en cuenta competiciones como la Premier, Bundesliga, Serie A, LaLiga... vuelve loco a todos los aficionados que se dan cita en las gradas del Stadionul Dinamo y que ya tienen a Martín Pascual como uno de sus ídolos.

articles.title: Zinedine Zidane, como Alejandro Sanz, con el 'Corazón partío'
articles.standfirst: Por tercera vez se enfrentan dos de sus hijos (Luca y Theo) sobre el verde de Butarque
articles.summary: Por tercera vez se enfrentan dos de sus hijos (Luca y Theo) sobre el verde de Butarque
articles.body: La familia Zidane vive el fútbol de forma intensa, pero cuando se enfrentan sus hijos, la intensidad se convierte en nerviosismo. Por tercera vez, el meta Luca Zidane y el centrocampista Theo Zidane se ven las caras sobre un rectángulo de juego en Segunda. Sobre el verde de Butarque tuvo lugar el enfrentamiento. Y, como siempre, Zinedine Zidane tiene el 'Corazón partío' a lo Alejandro Sanz. Luca fue titular en el once pepinero, mientras que Theo comenzó el partido desde el banquillo. Antes, los dos hermanos se saludaron, hablaron sobre el campo a su llegada al estadio. Una amabilidad que se 'olvida' durante los 90 minutos. Leganés y Córdoba no pasan por su mejor momento y, aunque los Zidanes siempre apostaron por el empate en el partido de sus hijos (de no ser que uno de los equipos estuviese muy necesitado de puntos o mirando hacia el ascenso), los tres puntos de Butarque se antojaban claves para ambos contendientes. Hay que recordar que Luca y Theo se han enfrentado dos veces en Segunda en la 2024-25, donde en el estadio de El Arcángel el Córdoba ganó 5-0 al Granada y donde el meta Luca encajó cinco goles. Mientras que en Los Cármenes, Theo vio la roja en el minuto 41 del encuentro.

articles.title: El Córdoba encuentra el premio al final y hunde al Lega en Butarque
articles.standfirst: Un gol de Eder García tras jugadón de Carracedo hace justicia, agrava la crisis pepinera y en el añadido fue expulsado Morata
articles.summary: Un gol de Eder García tras jugadón de Carracedo hace justicia, agrava la crisis pepinera y en el añadido fue expulsado Morata
articles.body: La crisis del Leganés se agrava. El conjunto pepinero volvió a tropezar en Butarque, esta vez ante un gran Córdoba y encadena cuatro derrotas consecutivas sin marcar un solo gol. Eder García hizo justicia con un Córdoba superior que firma así su segundo triunfo a domicilio. Cero puntos de los últimos 12 y una dinámica que empieza a ser alarmante. El equipo de Rubén Albés, que se quedó con uno menos en el añadido por la doble amarilla de Morata, sigue sin encontrar respuestas y la confianza en el proyecto empieza a ponerse a prueba. Ni los cambios introducidos por Albés en el once titular sirvieron para cambiar el rumbo. El técnico apostó por Kechta en el centro del campo, Pulido en defensa y Soko como referencia ofensiva, pero el Leganés volvió a mostrar sus dificultades para generar peligro y encontrar el camino del gol. La necesidad de ganar terminó convirtiéndose en otra noche de frustración para los pepineros, pese a los intentos de Rubén Pulido y Soko. Pero el duelo entró en una fase de igualdad y tedio que no lograron romper ni Naim con un tiro muy desviado ni Percan al que Ignasi Miquel taponó su disparo, mientras Diego Bri mandó cerca del poste el remate del córner. Antes del descanso Luca Zidane provocó una falta al borde del área grande tras hacerse un lío con el balón, pero el Córdoba la desperdició con una acción de estrategia que no le funcionó... fiel reflejo de lo que fue esta primera parte. Justo antes de la pausa Percan y Eder García probaron fortuna también para un Córdoba que acabó mejor. Tras la pausa el equipo andaluz siguió mejor que el madrileño y Percan, prolongando un gran pase de Carracedo, puso a prueba a un Luca Zidane que reaccionó metiendo una gran mano... lo mismo que poco después a un potente derechazo de Isma Ruiz que entraba junto al larguero. El siguiente en intentarlo fue Ghailan, pero entre Pulido e Ignasi Miquel taponaron su remate. Un triple cambio de Rubén Albés, dando entrada a Morata, Franquesa y Dani Rodríguez, animó al Lega y no tardó Zico en generar una acción de peligro. Pero ni él ni Diego Bri acertaron... hasta que en la recta final Eder García, con un disparo con mucho efecto dentro del área tras una gran jugada de Carracedo, decidió el encuentro. El equipo volvió a quedarse a cero, mientras el tiempo y los puntos siguen escapándose. La noche terminó de torcerse con la expulsión de Morata, que vio dos tarjetas amarillas tras salir en el minuto 63 y dejó a su equipo con diez jugadores en los últimos instantes. Butarque volvió a marcharse sin celebrar un gol y con una preocupación creciente. Cuatro partidos, cuatro derrotas y ningún tanto a favor. Una racha que obliga al Leganés a reaccionar cuanto antes. Butarque fue blanquiverde, en un triunfo grande de los de Ania.

articles.title: Morata ve la primera roja en su andadura en Segunda por protestón
articles.standfirst: En los minutos 70 y 91 vio las dos amarillas y el delantero del Lega fue expulsado por Eder Mallo
articles.summary: En los minutos 70 y 91 vio las dos amarillas y el delantero del Lega fue expulsado por Eder Mallo
articles.body: Corría el minuto 91 del partido Leganés- Córdoba cuando el colegiado Eder Mallo enseñó la segunda tarjeta amarilla a Morata. La primera, el delantero la vio en el minuto 70. Roja y Morata al vestuario antes del final del choque y el Leganés afrontando el tiempo de prolongación con 10 y perdiendo 0-1 con el Córdoba. Protestar le costó la segunda amarilla, lo que significó la primera expulsión de Morata en su andadura en Segunda. La primera tarjeta fue en el minuto 70 por encararse con Isma Ruiz tras un rifi-rafe dentro del área. Morata saltó al rectángulo de juego en el minuto 63 del partido sustituyendo a Soko y a los pocos minutos de estar sobre el verde ya vio su primera amonestación. Lo que nunca podía pensar es que no acabaría el partido por protestar.

articles.title: Off the Cuff: It’s time for the Buckeyes to take back control of the Big Ten
articles.summary: Saturday is a massive opportunity for Ohio State to reclaim its spot atop the Big Ten
articles.body:
First of all, I am extremely impressed with what Curt Cignetti has done with the Indiana Hoosiers football program. Their meteoric rise to the top of the college football world is something I've never seen before in the sport. Whether you're an Indiana fan or not, what they have done in such a short time is incredibly admirable.

Once the Buckeyes were knocked out of the College Football Playoff last year, I rooted for Indiana. My Uncle went there in the 90s. My cousin is a current student there.

Those family connections, combined with the incredible story the Hoosiers have been in college football the last two-plus years, are why I rooted for them in the Playoff last year. Before 2024, I never thought Indiana would win the national championship in college football.

That said, this offseason I've had a recurring feeling that Ohio State is looking up at Indiana in the Big Ten and nationally. It's a weird feeling.

Looking up at Indiana. Not Michigan, or Penn State, or any other historic Big Ten powerhouse. The Buckeyes are trying to unseat Indiana. Keep in mind, last year the Hoosiers beat the Buckeyes for the first time since 1988. This is Ohio State looking up at Indiana on the Big Ten and college football throne. Weird, right?

It's time for the Buckeyes to take back control of the Big Ten.

Since 2024, Oregon and Indiana have won the Big Ten. Oregon joined the Big Ten in 2024 and won the conference in their first season, and Indiana… well, they were irrelevant before Cignetti arrived in Bloomington.

Michigan winning three straight Big Ten titles is one thing, but seeing a Big Ten newcomer and Indiana win the next two Big Ten titles? That shouldn't sit well with any Ohio State fan.

That's why Saturday is an opportunity for the Buckeyes to take back control of the Big Ten. Go into Indiana and make a statement that their time is done atop the conference. It's been six years since Ohio State won the B1G Championship.

So much has happened since then. What if Ohio State goes into Bloomington and makes an absolute statement against the reigning national champions?

Indiana is not as dominant as they were last year. This is a really good Hoosiers team, but they're not as great as last year's team. They have been playing with their food way too much in Big Ten play.

The Hoosiers barely beat Northwestern at home, and they trailed Nebraska 17-6 early in the fourth quarter last week. Not to mention, they only led Western Kentucky 7-0 late in the first half in Week 3.

Statistically, the Hoosiers are similar, if not better, than last year in every yardage category on both sides of the ball. They've regressed in time of possession and third-down conversions. That's where Ohio State can have an advantage, especially if they're able to run the ball on offense and shut down the running game on defense.

One thing Ohio State will have to do Saturday is turn Indiana over. Josh Hoover has not thrown an interception this season. The Hoosiers have only lost one fumble. One turnover through six games. That's incredible.

But again, it just feels like the Hoosiers haven't been as dominant as they were last year. Last year, they won only three Big Ten games, including the Big Ten Championship, by one score. This year, they've already had to win two Big Ten games by one score.

Meanwhile, Ohio State has handled each of their first three Big Ten opponents by at least 17 points. They've won their first three Big Ten games by an average of 23 points. Indiana has won their first three games by an average of 13.7 points per game.

Even without Austin Siereveld and Ja'Kobi Jackson on Saturday, I still think the Buckeyes can run the ball. If they can, that will set up deep shot opportunities for Jeremiah Smith. One deep shot alone may change this game.

Plus, the Buckeyes know what happened in Indianapolis last year. They want revenge. Even if they don't say it, this game means more to them than every other game besides Michigan. That matters going into Saturday.

Revenge will be served. It's time for the Buckeyes to take back control of the Big Ten.

Game Prediction: Buckeyes 34 — Hoosiers 24

articles.title: Burnley 1-2 Wolves: Fer Lopez on target as Clarets' winless run at Turf Moor extends to 21 league games
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Burnley and Wolves at Turf Moor on Friday; Jamie Vardy scores first goal since returning to English football - but Fer Lopez and Tawanda Chirewa score to ensure Clarets' winless home run goes on
articles.body:
On October 18, it will be 12 months to the day since they beat Leeds 2-0 in the Premier League.

Since then, they have lost 11 games and drawn the other 10. It is the longest run without a home win across England's top four tiers.

Jamie Vardy's first English football goal since returning last month put Nicky Hayen's side ahead, but defensive errors allowed Fer Lopez and Tawanda Chirewa to turn the game around, securing Wolves' first win in three and lifting them to sixth.

In an interview with Sky Sports earlier this week , Vardy had been asked if this was his final season as a professional. "We'll have to wait until the summer and let my legs tell my head what they think!" he said.

On Friday night, Vardy proved his legs still have plenty left in them.

The 39-year-old found the net with his second shot of the game, scoring his first goal in English football since May 18, 2025, when he netted his 200th and final goal for Leicester.

But his strike was not enough to send Burnley into half-time ahead. Kyle Walker gifted possession away just outside his own penalty area, and Wolves were quick to punish the costly error.

Sean Neave took over, squaring the ball for Lopez to fire home via the inside of the left-hand post.

Burnley lost their grip on the game after the break and fell behind with 18 minutes remaining. Igor's dreadful touch gifted Chirewa the opportunity to strike, and although his effort was met by Gregoire Coudert's gloves, the ball looped over the goalkeeper and under the crossbar.

Burnley offered little in response and were met with a chorus of boos at the final whistle, as their fifth league defeat of the season was confirmed.
